# Challenger House

> Organisational Architecture for the AI transition. Nobody wrote down how you actually lead. Every function in your company is being redesigned for AI, except the one that runs them all: management. That gap is the missing middle, and Challenger House builds it with your leadership team, with frontier AI, on real work.

Every function in your company is being redesigned for AI. Except the one that runs them all: management. That is the missing middle. Challenger House builds it with you, by writing down how you actually work: your leadership team, frontier AI, one real piece of management work, live, in a day. Once it is written down, AI can finally work on it, and so can you.

We are three operators (Marcus Druen, André Cramer, Brittney Bean) with three decades of organisational development, facilitation and venture building, now turned on the AI transition. We spark courage to act now.

## The missing middle

You run two organisations: the formal one you wrote down, and the informal one that actually gets the work done. AI only knows the first. Between them sits everything your company runs on but never built. Three floors, all empty:

- Never written down: how decisions really get made, how handovers really work, where judgment really sits. None of it is encoded, so AI cannot touch it, and every licence you bought is reading the org chart instead.
- Unwritten for good reasons: this is the organisational shadow, the people and the politics. Ambiguity protects options, positions and peace, which is why this is leadership work with the team in the room, not a documentation project to delegate.
- Never remembered: every AI pilot reveals something true about how the company actually works, but without a learning loop none of it is captured, every pilot starts from zero, and nothing compounds.

Challenger House builds the missing middle: the organisation written down, honestly enough for people to recognise it, precisely enough for AI to run on it, and with the learning loop that keeps it alive.

## The offer (one hour, one day, one quarter)

- One hour, free, 1:1 remote: bring the problem that keeps coming back. We work it live, with AI as your sparring partner. You leave seeing your missing middle for the first time.
- [The 1-Day Experience](https://www.challenger.house/one-day.html): four figures, your leadership team, one value stream. Your team takes one real piece of management work, the board paper, the investment decision, the steering meeting, and rebuilds it with frontier AI, live in the room. You leave with working artefacts (workflows redesigned, first MVPs, a backlog of use cases, the start of a business case) and something no licence can buy: your team has felt what AI does to its own thinking and judgment.
- [The Build](https://www.challenger.house/build.html): five figures, three months, your team. Three months wrapped around a three-day Residency, so the backlog gets built, the unwritten gets written, and the learning loop closes: what every week reveals is captured, so capability compounds until the new way of working survives Monday. A living Org Mirror comes with it.

## The three gaps we close

- The imagination gap: leaders cannot act on capabilities they have never experienced, and for most leadership teams generative AI means Copilot, so the ambition starts too low. If the top does not use it, the top cannot judge it.
- The decision gap: the work below leadership keeps accelerating while the management system does not. Decisions still travel through the Monday jour fixe, the hundred-slide deck, the meeting about the meeting. Management has been digitised, not yet redesigned for AI.
- The operating gap: every company runs two organisations, formal and informal, and they drift further apart with every pilot. What each pilot reveals is never captured, so nothing compounds, licences sit idle, and pilots die in meetings.

## Who we work with

Our clients are challengers. They'd rather shape what's coming than have it happen to them. They know the next challenger in their market will be AI-native: leaner, flatter, faster, and the race that matters runs between incumbents, who closes the gap first. They know Copilot is where the race starts, not where it is won. They treat this as a complex change process, 80% people and 20% tools, and lead it themselves, with or without AI in their title.
